about.text: Once one of Banbury's most prestigious exports, and nationally famous, its production went into decline by the 18th-century, and eventually ceased. The cheese is best known today through an insult in Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor (1597). Pictured is a 15th/16th-century recipe for Banbury cheese.

sources.text: Historic, no longer made; soft, rich, creamy thin rounds with a skin; new and ripe stages existed but no durations recorded
